current_focus.domain: media-library-014: where the images of repoglance.com live and how editors manage them; EmDash's Media Library with image fields and dark variants in place of repository-owned static files picked by slug; serving, bootstrap, import, the imagery rules as an audit of what is live; the pattern commerce will follow
current_focus.summary: Maintainer 'agree on all; lock it and spawn the session' on 2026-10-07 after a frontier batch grilled against WooCommerce. Bounded implementation of media-library-014, to be built by a fresh session: (1) seed/seed.json: hero and feature block types get an image field (darkVariant) in place of the screenshot select, the pages' blocks reference the captures, and the seed declares the 26 captures as $media for bootstrap; the content tests follow. (2) src/components/Screenshot.astro and Hero.astro render from the media reference with EmDash's Image component or the image endpoint, the dark source from darkVariant, alt from the media item with a fallback to the heading, no figure when the reference is gone; the home hero keeps the band policy. (3) src/namespace-gate.ts and the guard admit anonymous GET on the public media-file route and the image endpoint, cached at the edge like the pages, everything else unchanged; smoke and guard tests follow. (4) scripts/cms-media.mjs: --check lists the library against the approved captures (hash, alt, dimensions, dark pairing) and --apply uploads the missing files with alt through the media API, recording the source hash; identity as the other CMS scripts. (5) The mirror (src/cms/mirror.ts, scripts/cms-mirror.mjs) also writes seed/media.json, the media manifest, and tests/content.test.mjs judges it (approved captures only, honest alt, no fixture code, no live data). (6) cms:sync carries the breaking block-type change. (7) docs/content.md, docs/cms-access.md, README, design.md note and AGENTS.md follow; the SmokySkills reference is updated separately. Verification: unit tests, npm run verify, a dev-server round trip (setup from the seed with $media, the library listing the captures, the pages rendering from media references with light and dark sources, an admin-style image swap mirrored into the manifest, the migration script's --check and --apply against the dev server), browser captures of both pages in both schemes compared with the current site, a separate read-only review on the exact commit, ledger records, commit with the trailer, push, PR against main. Maintainer gates after merge: deploy, cloudflared access login, npm run cms:sync (the breaking block-type change), npm run cms:media -- --apply, npm run check:live. No merge, deploy, Cloudflare, DNS, Access or secret action by the agent.

decisions.question: How do seed/seed.json (copy, imagery slots, block types) and the EmDash CMS on repoglance.com stay equal, so the live site never silently diverges from the locked content again: which is the source, how does it reach the other, with which identity and trigger, and what proves the live site equals the seed?
decisions.rationale: Maintainer's answer 'D' to the four options presented with their gates and costs. Facts behind the shape: EmDash 1.0.1's client and CLI accept a cloudflared-cached Access JWT (cf-access-token), so the maintainer's own identity drives the API with no new Cloudflare resource; a service-token JWT carries no email and would need a Service Auth policy, a service token, an EmDash API token and a guard change (documented as the unattended option, not built); removing a select option is a breaking block-type change in EmDash 1.0.1, so the sync creates and activates a new version and migrates the blocks; the CMS must be written only after the Worker that renders the new seed is deployed, so the trigger is the deploy runbook, never the merge. Options A (seed only), B (sync without the live check) and C (CMS as source, seed exported) were not chosen. Builds on the closed track's site-copy-006, site-imagery-007 and cms-access-008 (.grilltrack/archive/gt-20261001102301-89ec89/).

decisions.choice: CMS-first (maintainer, 2026-10-07, with four amendments). (1) The CMS owns content: an edit published in the EmDash admin is live and persists; nothing ever writes copy from seed/seed.json into the CMS after the one-time bootstrap. (2) The repository owns structure: block types, components, image slugs, the Worker; they reach the CMS by deploy and a schema-only sync. (3) The site mirrors itself into the repository on publish and unpublish, with no schedule: after answering the admin's request the Worker builds the seed from the CMS, pushes a branch and opens a PR titled 'CMS edit: ...' labelled cms-edit through a GitHub fine-grained token scoped to this repository that may push a branch and open a PR and never merges; a repository workflow arms auto-merge for cms-edit PRs and branch protection lets them merge only when the checks are green; a published edit that fails a truth test leaves its PR open and red. (4) If the mirror fails for any reason (GitHub unreachable, token error, anything) the Worker sends a failure email to agent@smokyproduct.co naming the page, the error and how to re-run npm run cms:mirror; it never fails silently; npm run cms:mirror is the manual and on-touch safety net (every agent session and the schema sync start with it). (5) Agents only write drafts, never publish: a machine identity (Access service token plus a draft-scoped EmDash API token) is admitted by the namespace gate only to read and to write drafts; publish, unpublish, schedule, delete and schema writes answer 404 to it; the agent hands the maintainer EmDash's preview link and the admin link, and the maintainer edits and publishes in the admin. (6) Before writing a draft the agent reads the page's current revision and writes against it: the gate refuses a machine draft write that carries no _rev, and EmDash refuses one whose _rev is stale (409), so the agent re-reads and redoes the draft on the newer version. (7) A brand-new site's first CMS load comes from the seed through EmDash setup, once.

decisions.question: Who owns the content of repoglance.com, who owns its structure, how does the repository learn about edits made in the EmDash admin, what may an agent do in the CMS, what happens when the mirror fails, and how is a fresh site bootstrapped?
decisions.rationale: Replaces cms-sync-011 (option D), reopened on the maintainer's instruction: an admin who logs in to make a change expects it to persist, and people letting agents build will want to log in and override. Alternatives weighed: E (admin wins, repo follows through an export PR, conflict-aware sync) kept two writers of content and a manual export; a scheduled mirror was rejected for a site edited months apart; agents editing the CMS directly without a human gate was rejected because the truth rules exist to stop unproven claims. EmDash 1.2 facts behind the shape: no outbound webhooks but host hooks on publish/unpublish and waitUntil in the Worker; roles have no edit-any-without-publish tier and tokens belong to the user who creates them, so the draft-only rule lives in our gate; PUT /content accepts _rev and answers 409 on a stale revision.

decisions.choice: EmDash's Media Library (maintainer, 2026-10-07, grilled against WooCommerce's model). (1) The two pages' pictures move into the Media Library; the hero and feature block types replace the screenshot select with an image field carrying a darkVariant; the Open Graph image and the mark stay build products. (2) Alt text lives on the media item, with a render-time fallback to the block's own heading; the imagery rules audit the library's alt. (3) Serving through the Worker: the namespace guard admits the public media-file route and the image endpoint, edge-cached like the pages; the image endpoint serves the widths from one source per capture (the hand-cut 540 and 1080 files retire), with a visual capture confirming the crops; a public bucket or CDN is a later option. (4) Import like WooCommerce's: a migration script uploads the 26 files (13 captures, dark and light) once with their alt text, records each file's hash as the source and skips files already present; the seed declares the same files as $media so a fresh site sideloads them at bootstrap. (5) Any uploaded image may be used on a page; the mirror writes a media manifest next to the seed (id, hash, alt, dimensions, dark pairing) and the repository's tests judge it on the mirror PR, red when a rule breaks (approved captures only, honest alt, no fixture code, no live data). (6) darkVariant replaces the -light file naming; the home hero's follows-the-band policy stays in the component. (7) A block whose image reference is gone renders no figure and the audit flags it. (8) Commerce follows the same pattern later: a primary image, an ordered gallery, a variation image falling back to the product's, a store placeholder, named size presets, API shapes with src, srcset, sizes and alt; a media plugin is only WooCommerce's extension layer (bulk and feed import deduped by source and hash, CDN offload, regeneration, video) talking to the library's API, never its own store; alt stored on the item with a render-time fallback to the product name.
decisions.domain: media-library-014: where the images of repoglance.com live and how editors manage them; EmDash's Media Library with image fields and dark variants in place of repository-owned static files picked by slug; serving, bootstrap, import, the imagery rules as an audit of what is live; the pattern commerce will follow

decisions.question: Where do the images of repoglance.com live and how does an editor manage them, now that the CMS owns content: repository-owned static files picked by a select of slugs (the admin's Media page empty), or EmDash's Media Library with image fields, and with which serving path, bootstrap, import, rules, dark pairing and fallback?
decisions.rationale: The admin is the editor's whole view of the site; imagery the editor cannot find under Content > Media reads as broken and cannot be acted on. WooCommerce, read in its documentation and source (the product-images doc, the v3 REST products controller, the product importer, wc-product-functions.php, WC_Regenerate_Images, the Store API image schema), owns no files: products reference the platform's Media Library, alt lives on the attachment with a render-time fallback, sizes are named presets regenerated in the background and on demand, every import path sideloads into the library and records the source, and extensions are a layer on top. EmDash has every equivalent piece (the Media Library on R2 with content hashes, image/gallery/media/video fields, darkVariant, the Image component and image endpoint, $media in seeds). The static path shipped under site-imagery-007 protected repository tests; those rules move to a manifest the mirror writes and do not disappear.
